title: bonsai.check/1
description: bonsai check --json (spec §6, findings and warnings; spec §3, §16 row 29): what check found in a project. Printed, never stored. Written by bonsai check --json; read by CI, rung 0, agents and the studio, now that Bonsai has no screens of its own. Any finding makes check exit 1; warnings never change the exit code. When check cannot run (exit 2 or 3), findings and warnings are [] and error says why. With --write (step 5.1.8) check rebuilds the two tables, in the main checkout only: in a worktree it refuses, exit 4, its error naming the main checkout; and its exit code then says only whether it wrote (0 written, 3 it could not), the findings listed but changing nothing (spec §6). Later steps add fields as additions (check --write's result among them). A writer writes every field below, in this order, null, [] or {} where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one and refuses a duplicate key.

format.description: The version, always the first field (contract §2.2).

findings.description: What check found (spec §6, bonsai check findings), in the order check looks; [] for none.

examples.message: work/protocols/session-start.md was edited since Bonsai wrote it

code.description: What it is, a fixed word: an open list. Its known words live in Bonsai's one table of findings and warnings (step 5.1.6), which bonsai check --schema bonsai.check prints; this schema does not copy them, and a reader shows a word it does not know as other.

file.description: The project file it is about, project-relative with forward slashes; null when it is about no one file.

message.description: What is wrong, one sentence for a person, in ASCII.
examples: work/protocols/session-start.md was edited since Bonsai wrote it

next.description: The next thing to do and who does it, as the error object's next is (bonsai.error).

do.description: What to do: the command to run, written run: and the command line, or the step in plain words.
examples: open Claude Code in this checkout and accept its trust question

who.description: Who does it, a closed list: agent (any agent may do it, unattended) or person (a person's step: a consent such as --allow-exec, a tap, a setting, an install, or a command an agent's task does not grant it; spec §4, §6).

warnings.description: What check warns of (spec §6, Warnings): printed, never changing the exit code, never a rung's colour or a status --json problem; [] for none.

examples.message: .bonsai/tasks.md differs from what check --write would write

next.do: run: bonsai check --write in the main checkout

code.description: What went wrong, as a fixed word: an open list (contract §2.2). Later steps add words, which is an addition (format review 4.5), and a reader shows a word it does not know as other. The known words live in one table in Bonsai's code, their one home, which bonsai check --schema bonsai.error prints (and, from step 5.1.10, the reference page of lists, docs/reference/lists.md); this schema does not copy them, and the words in its examples are illustrative.
